problem: The pricing page matched lifecycle and SaaS tiers but still omitted several customer-visible Portal V2 capability domains, creating an incomplete commercial representation of the product.
root_cause: Parity checks focused on lifecycle, tier entitlements and checkout semantics instead of maintaining a customer-visible capability inventory against canonical Portal V2 source modules.
prevention: Pricing must expose the customer-relevant Portal V2 capability domains, including assurance, impact, execution, compliance, resource intelligence and decision governance.
A regression test must verify both the pricing claims and the canonical source modules that ground those claims.
Future portal capability additions must be reviewed for commercial-surface impact rather than assuming lifecycle/tier parity is sufficient.

evidence.outcome: Pricing now carries an explicit customer-facing Portal V2 capability contract in addition to lifecycle and plan entitlement parity.
